config.title: Color Picker

intro.title: Color Picker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive color picker application using Vue.js. You will learn how to use Vue's reactive data system to manage and update a color value in real-time. The main technologies involved are Vue's ref for state management, computed properties for derived values, and event handling to respond to user input. By the end, you'll have a functional component that displays a selected color and allows users to change it through a color input.
intro.usecase: Color pickers are essential UI components in design tools, content management systems, and customization interfaces. You'll find them in applications like Figma or Adobe Photoshop for selecting design colors, in WordPress themes for customizing site appearances, and in e-commerce platforms where users personalize products. As a Vue developer, implementing color pickers helps you build interactive forms, dashboard settings panels, and user preference sections that require visual selection interfaces.

objectives: Construct a reactive color state using Vue's ref API
Implement a color input element and bind it to the reactive state
Configure a color preview display that updates dynamically with the selected color
Apply computed properties to convert hex color values to RGB format
Integrate multiple color input methods (hex, RGB sliders) into a single component
Manipulate the DOM to display real-time color changes in the preview area
Initialize a color picker component with default values and validation

steps.instruction: Add a div element below the paragraph that displays the selectedColor value. Set its background-color style to the selectedColor value and give it a fixed width and height to create a visual color swatch.
steps.hint: Use the style attribute to set background-color to selectedColor. Add width and height properties like '100px' to make the swatch visible.

successCriteria: A div element is added with style attribute setting background-color to selectedColor and includes width and height properties.

steps.instruction: In the template, use v-for to create a button element for each color in the colorOptions array. Each button should display its color value as text.
steps.hint: Use v-for="color in colorOptions" on a button element, and output {{ color }} inside the button.

// Similar: rendering list items
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain a button for each color option, displaying the hex code as text.
successCriteria: A button element with v-for iterating over colorOptions is added to the template, and each button shows its color value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button uses v-for and displays the color value correctly.

steps.title: Wire color buttons to the selection handler
steps.instruction: Add a click event handler to each color button in your v-for loop that calls the selectColor function with the corresponding color value.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive on each button element to trigger the selectColor handler with the current color from the loop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding click handlers to buttons in a list
<button v-for="item in items" @click="handleClick(item)">{{ item }}</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each color button will now respond to clicks and update the selected color state when clicked.
successCriteria: All color buttons have @click handlers that call selectColor with their respective color values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure each button in the v-for loop has an @click handler that calls selectColor with the current color value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The color buttons aren't properly connected to the selection handler. Check that you've added @click="selectColor(color)" to each button element.
